solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bed covers medium for cosiness (7)

indicators.note: to cover is to lie over and enclose, so the bed wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
M = medium, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A shopping note about bedding chosen to make a bedroom feel snug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed covers' reads as duvets and quilts, but 'covers' is a verb: the bed wraps round the other pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun for physical ease and warmth stands in for cosiness.

entries.clue: Fresh sandwiches are transformed by soft cheese (10)

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between two halves, like bread round a filling
to transform is to change the form, so ARE takes a new order

blocks.note: a fresh wind is a chilly one

annotation.surface: A deli boast that fresh sandwiches are lifted by a soft cheese filling.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'sandwiches' food, but it is a verb, and 'Fresh' is the weather sense. Caerphilly is a Welsh town as well as its cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a crumbly white Welsh cheese named after its home town.

entries.clue: School examiner? (6,9)

blocks.note: reads as a place of learning; the setter means a school of fish
reads as someone who sets exam papers; here a scientist who studies creatures, the question mark flagging the pun

annotation.surface: A school inspector checking up on a classroom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' wants to mean a place of learning, making the examiner an inspector; here it is a school of fish, studied by a scientist of sea life.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue as a definition: a scientist whose subjects include schools of fish.

entries.clue: Roman port of old with islands to the north (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: an ait is a small river island

annotation.surface: A history note on an ancient Roman harbour with islands off to its north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roman port of old' reads as one definition, but 'of' only links and 'old' gives O. Aits are islets in a river, a word met mostly on the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the ancient harbour city at the Tiber's mouth that served Rome.

entries.clue: Sample clothes newly lined in the latest style (8)

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap round a body, so TRY dresses the letters inside it
'newly' means made afresh, so LINED is set out in a new order

annotation.surface: A fashion tip: try on clothes with fresh linings, cut in this season's look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sample clothes' looks like trying on garments; 'clothes' is a verb, one piece dressing another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fashionably, following whatever style is newest.

entries.clue: Side of duck prepared for gourmets (7)

indicators.note: ingredients are prepared by chopping and mixing, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

annotation.surface: A restaurant menu line: a side of duck, made for discerning diners.
annotation.walkthrough: Duck looks like the dish, but it is the cricketer's nought, O.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: people who love eating well, a looser modern word for gourmets.

entries.clue: Trousers and blazers used in emergencies (6)

blocks.note: bell-bottomed trousers, widening from the knee
things that blaze: bright signals fired from a ship in distress

annotation.surface: A clothing list pairing trousers with blazers kept for emergencies.
annotation.walkthrough: Next to 'Trousers', 'blazers' wants to be jackets; here it means things that blaze.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: wide-bottomed seventies trousers, and the bright signals fired in distress.

entries.clue: Shots of batsmen after stripping off extra gear (9)

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layer, so the phrase loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: a cover drive is a cricket stroke through the off side; drop the outer C and S

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: batsmen's strokes once they have taken off extra kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gear' in a cricket setting suggests pads and gloves, but it is a car's gear.
annotation.definitionFit: A motoring term: a gear above top that cuts engine revs at speed, so an extra one.

entries.clue: At the front with gunners vulnerable to attack (2,3,6,4)

blocks.note: the literal sense: in the rank of soldiers doing the shooting
the figurative sense: exposed to criticism or blame

annotation.surface: A soldier's position alongside the artillery, exposed to enemy fire.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves describe battle, so the join is hard to see; the second is the everyday figurative sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: literally in the soldiers' front rank, figuratively exposed to blame or attack.

entries.clue: Bag with zip, not a hit (4)

indicators.note: 'with' means accompanied by, so O is brought into the word
'not a' says the A is absent, leaving the gap the O fills

blocks.note: the letter swapped out of SACK

annotation.surface: A shopper sizing up a zipped bag that has not been a best-seller.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Zip' suggests a fastener, but it is slang for nothing, and 'hit' is not a best-seller but a blow.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: to punch or strike someone forcefully.

entries.clue: Pine endlessly for attention (3)

indicators.note: 'endlessly' read literally means without ends, so both ends go

blocks.note: to pine is to yearn; take off Y and N

annotation.surface: Someone craving attention and never letting up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' reads as 'forever' but takes both ends off the word.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have someone's ear, or lend an ear, is to have or give attention.

entries.clue: Healing cure that I merged with PE (11)

indicators.note: merged things are blended into one, so the letters mix into a new order

annotation.surface: A school notion that a cure works best combined with physical education.
annotation.walkthrough: PE stands for physical education, the school gym lesson; here it is just two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having curative power, doing the body good.

entries.clue: Is trying on nail polish an unpleasant feeling? (4,3,7)

indicators.note: in an across entry, a piece put on another comes after it

blocks.note: a pin is a slender nail
to sand is to polish smooth
something trying irritates, which is what needling does

annotation.surface: A question whether testing a nail varnish gives you a queasy sensation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nail polish' is two separate words here, and 'Is trying' is a verb that goes last.
annotation.definitionFit: A named sensation: the prickling tingle in a limb as numbness wears off.

entries.clue: Risk period stimulated net gain (10)

indicators.note: stimulated means stirred up, so NET is shaken into a new order

blocks.note: to risk money is to bet it
a term is a period of time

annotation.surface: A trader's report: a risky stretch spurred a net profit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Net gain' reads as a financial phrase, but 'net' belongs to the wordplay and 'gain' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: improvement, a gain in one's condition.

entries.clue: Inane writer’s rancour about City (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so BILE surrounds EC

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

annotation.surface: A columnist's silly bitterness towards the financial world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is the setter speaking of himself. The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival use: a word usually met as a noun for a fool, here meaning stupid.

entries.clue: Bad press about crime, mostly it is made up (9)

indicators.note: 'mostly' means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
made up means invented or put together, so the letters are assembled anew

annotation.surface: A complaint that newspaper coverage of crime is largely invented.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a grumble about tabloids; the definition is just 'Bad press', and everything after it is anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unfavourable comment, which is what bad press amounts to.

entries.clue: Lovely guess (6)

blocks.note: as a verb, to discover by intuition

annotation.surface: An admiring 'lovely guess!' after a lucky answer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two words together as praise; split them, and each is a separate sense of one word, an adjective and a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: heavenly in the gushing sense, and to intuit or foretell as a verb.

entries.clue: Excited as always tucking into salmon? (8)

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, as a diner tucks into a meal, so EVER goes in

blocks.note: salmon is one example of a fish, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: Someone who gets thrilled every time they tuck into salmon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' only links, and the question mark admits that salmon is merely one kind of the thing wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: agitated, worked up as if running a temperature.

entries.clue: One in a shower cap coating one in a lather (6)

indicators.note: a coating covers all round, so LID encloses the other letters
to be in a lather is to be agitated, so ONE is stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: Bathroom business: someone in the shower with a cap, soaping up.
annotation.walkthrough: The shower is a meteor shower, not a bathroom one: the Leonids appear every November.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a meteor of the November shower that seems to radiate from Leo.

entries.clue: Luther’s the cause one’s left abandoned (8)

indicators.note: Luther was German, so 'Luther's the' is the German word for the
'left' as in departed: one, I, has gone from the word

blocks.note: to elicit is to bring about, cause
one = I, the letter removed from ELICIT

annotation.surface: Martin Luther's cause, once his followers have deserted it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Luther's the cause' looks like a statement about the Reformation; it asks for 'the' in Luther's German.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: left to fall into ruin by its owners.

entries.clue: Delays unlikely aboard ship (6)

indicators.note: aboard means inside a vessel, so TALL goes inside SS

blocks.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

annotation.surface: A reassurance that holdups are not expected on board.
annotation.walkthrough: TALL means unlikely only in phrases like 'a tall tale'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a verb in the third person, holds things up or puts them off.

entries.clue: Selfish person’s party spirit, other people temper (3,2,3,6)

annotation.surface: A killjoy whose party mood makes others lose their tempers.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', joining definition to wordplay. The phrase comes from Aesop's fable of a dog lying in a manger to keep the cattle from hay it cannot eat.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from Aesop: someone who keeps from others what is of no use to themselves.

entries.clue: A cycling expert’s promise (5)

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter wheels round to the front

blocks.note: a guru is an expert; move its final U to the front

annotation.surface: A pledge from someone who knows all about bicycles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests a bike expert, but it rotates the expert's letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to portend or give promise of, as in 'augurs well'.

entries.clue: Passionate backing singer (4)

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the word reads in reverse

annotation.surface: A fervent backing vocalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing singer' is a stock phrase, but 'backing' belongs with 'Passionate'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a twist: a celebrated female opera star, often temperamental.

entries.clue: Making your mark, opening with underwear half-removed (11)

indicators.note: half-removed means half taken away, so only the first half of the word stays

blocks.note: only its first half, LING, is kept

annotation.surface: A saucy scene of someone making an impression by partly shedding underwear at a launch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a striptease; 'opening' is an adjective, not an event.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: signing with the first letters of one's names is literally making a mark.

entries.clue: Fish being skinless helped (3)

indicators.note: the skin is the outside, so the outer letters are peeled off

blocks.note: aided = helped; peel off the outer A and D

annotation.surface: A cook's note that the fish was served skinned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skinless' seems to describe the fish, but it strips the word after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a European freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the orfe.

entries.clue: Aunt Maud’s regularly drunk and falls (7)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
a drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: M, U, S: the odd letters of MAUDS

annotation.surface: A family story of an aunt who often drinks too much and topples over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like tumbles, which suits the tipsy aunt, but it is the American name for a season.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in American English the season is called fall.

entries.clue: Gathering in street after race victor enters (7)

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so ST is placed behind the rest
to enter is to go inside, so V goes into HARE

blocks.note: to hare is to race along
V = victor, from the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A crowd gathering in the street once the race winner arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Race' is a verb here, and 'victor' is not the winner but a radio code letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the gathering-in of a crop at season's end.
